short: Ensemble-to-student distillation (M02, M06, M13) is standard: same-modality distillation predates it; 85.9% is one unseeded split of unstated unit, and 7x smaller is against six models.
position: KDE-SSI [@lai2023kdessi] changes three components: a soft-voting ResNet1D ensemble supplies soft targets for a student (M02), the deployed decoder is that single student (M06), and its time and size are reported (M13). All three are standard: same-modality distillation of word classifiers was published for lip reading three years earlier [@ma2021towards]. The headline "7.0× smaller, 20.8× faster" compares the student with six models on a GPU (Fig. 5), so most of it follows from N = 6. The comparison that matters, the student against one ResNet1D (85.9% vs 81.2%, Table II), comes from one unseeded split whose grouping unit is not stated (§IV.E), with no student trained without a teacher. So 85.9% is not comparable with the later subject-independent 85.8% on the same words [@hong2026cvos], and the deployment claim (§V.B) has no device measurement.
